mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations and economic growth. This relationship holds across all monetary regimes without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The negative correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 3.0%, it signals imminent monetary easing that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 3.0%, the 20-day forward returns are not positive in more than 50% of cases (i.e., positive returns occur in <=50% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 3.0% and CPIAUCSL exceeds 210, the combination of accommodative policy and high inflation creates uncertainty that suppresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and low policy rates
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 210, the 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 50% of cases (i.e., negative returns occur in <=50% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000 thousand units, it signals weakening residential demand and economic contraction, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1000, the 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 50% of cases (i.e., negative returns occur in <=50% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects economic distress that reduces corporate earnings and risk appetite.
failure_condition: The negative correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high industrial production index (INDPRO) above 115 indicates strong economic activity that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The positive correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0), a low federal funds rate (below 3.0%) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as the central bank is likely to implement further rate cuts to stimulate the economy.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 5.0, the condition FEDFUNDS < 3.0% does not predict positive 20-day returns (i.e., returns are negative or not significantly positive).

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) falls below 380000 million dollars, it signals weakening consumer demand and economic slowdown, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 380000, the 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 50% of cases (i.e., negative returns occur in <=50% of instances).
